title: Make your own event-sourced agent harness using stream processors — Jonas Templestein, Iterate
talk_summary: Jonas Templestein demos an event-sourced agent harness built on a durable append-only event stream (events.iterate.com) where all agent behavior is a stream processor: a pure synchronous reducer over events plus an after-append hook for side effects. The live demo largely fails, but the architecture ideas (event log as single primitive, reducers separated from side effects, circuit-breaker processors, dynamic worker code-as-event, push subscriptions) are concrete and copyable.

takeaways.what_they_do: Agent logic is a synchronous reduce(state, event) -> state with no side effects; all side effects (LLM calls, appends) happen in a separate after-append hook, so a restarted processor catches up on state before deciding what to do.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you should not do side effects in this reduce function... if your program goes to sleep... you don't want your program to go and make a ton of LLM requests for all of those 100 events in the past

takeaways.what_they_do: A processor tracks timestamps of the last 100 events; if more than 100 arrive within a second it appends a 'paused' event, and further appends are rejected without generating error events.
takeaways.evidence_quote: if you put more than 100 events in a second or something, it is just going to circuit break and then the stream will be paused until somebody unpauses it

takeaways.what_they_do: Appending an event containing bundled JS source (a reducer + after-append hook) makes the stream itself run that processor on Cloudflare dynamic workers, with secrets injected outside the stream at fetch time.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can append that to any stream, and then that stream becomes an AI agent
takeaways.numbers: ~40 lines of code for a basic AI agent

takeaways.what_they_do: The stream can push events to a third-party HTTP endpoint (or pull via SSE), letting plugins run on other machines/languages and be woken when events need processing.
takeaways.evidence_quote: the stream can reach out to the processors and say, 'You got to do something, you know? You need to process some events now.'

takeaways.technique: Bounded-wait eventual consistency instead of before-hooks
takeaways.what_they_do: Rather than blocking before-hooks (which break context caching and add cost), the agent loop waits up to ~200ms for optional enrichment (safety checks, RAG context) then proceeds regardless.
takeaways.evidence_quote: we're going to wait for up to 200 milliseconds for somebody to say I've got a little bit of information for you, but then we're actually going to make the LLM request whether you come in with information or not

takeaways.technique: Composable reducers over shared event types
takeaways.what_they_do: Because reducers are pure synchronous functions, a processor can import another harness's reducer and event types and build on them for free.
takeaways.evidence_quote: you can just in your processor use their reducer. It's practically free, right? Like you can just import it and run it.
